h: East Leeds Escapes to Pair With Your Round
p: The Springs is part of Thorpe Park Leeds, a development on the eastern edge of the city right by the M1 and the A1(M) link. That makes it particularly handy for families coming in from places like Wakefield, Castleford, Garforth and beyond, as you can be parked up and putting without battling city-centre traffic. It's also a nice alternative for anyone who wants to avoid the busiest parts of town on a Saturday.

A round of mini golf is a great way to start or finish a trip, but east Leeds has some cracking days out within easy reach. Temple Newsam, a grand Tudor-Jacobean house set in vast parkland, is just a few miles away. As well as the house itself, there's Home Farm, a big working rare-breed farm where kids can meet pigs, goats, cattle and more, and acres of parkland and woodland to explore. Temple Newsam's grounds were landscaped by Capability Brown, and in late spring the rhododendron walks are a real picture, so it's worth timing a visit then if you can.

Head a bit further east and you'll find Lotherton, a country estate near Aberford with an Edwardian house, gardens, and a wildlife world with birds from around the globe, including flamingos. It's a lovely family day out, with plenty of space for picnics and play.

Back at The Springs, there's a choice of places to eat, so you can grab a bite before or after your round. And the open green space around Thorpe Park Leeds, with paths and water features, is perfect for a stroll. It's a cracking spot for a relaxed afternoon, combining crazy golf, food and a bit of fresh air.
